claims.text: Aging AlCoCrFeNi2.1 in the brittle regime produces a critical threshold of L12 ordering within the FCC matrix.
The critical L12 ordering maximizes antiphase boundary energy (APBE).
High APBE associated with L12 ordering restricts cross-slip and forces planar slip.
Jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries concentrate stress generated by localized planar slip.
Stress concentration at jagged B2/FCC interfaces exceeds their cohesive strength and causes brittle interfacial fracture.
Higher-temperature aging reduces the L12 order degree and APBE, thereby restoring cross-slip and ductile deformation.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a ductile dual-phase FCC and B2 microstructure.
The as-cast alloy has a homogeneous chemical distribution.
The as-cast alloy has smooth phase boundaries.
Aging at 600°C induces significant L12 ordering with local chemistry approaching stoichiometric Ni3Al.
Aging at 600°C promotes the development of jagged or serrated B2/FCC interfaces.
Ordering is maximized near 600°C, while diffusion is insufficient to coarsen the interfaces or substantially reduce ordering.
The as-cast state has low APBE, enabling easy cross-slip and uniform plastic deformation.
Aging at 600°C causes a sharp drop in elongation to failure.
The 600°C-aged alloy fractures intergranularly or along jagged phase boundaries.
Ductility recovers at 750°C because ordered domains dissolve or their order parameter decreases.
The brittle transition occurs when the L12 superlattice fraction raises APBE above the stress threshold for activating cross-slip.
The cited records concern Al1.5CoCrFeNi, CoNiCrFeMn, and Ag rather than AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The CoNiCrFeMn evidence attributes hindered partial-dislocation motion to lattice-parameter-mismatch friction.
The exact critical chemical-order parameter and the relative roles of boundary segregation and intrinsic APBE are not established by the cited records.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis calls the jagged B2/FCC boundaries pre-existing, whereas the initial-state and baseline fields describe smooth boundaries and the intervention says aging develops the jagged boundaries.
The hypothesis labels 550-750°C as the brittle window, but the conditions and predicted outcome identify 750°C as a recovered ductile state.
